slot_note: re-root after the v1 architecture was sent back at Gate C and Gate G; same number and objective
niche: night-time economy hotspot patrol slate off offences the force records as an occurrence window rather than a time, the window being bounded by the keeper's own last look and first notice, so which hours the record can see at all is set by the keeper's routine
stakeholder_role: community safety manager of a city partnership, who commissions the 2027 hotspot patrol slate

spine.row_meaning: one recorded offence, with the earliest and the latest time it can have occurred

world.geography: Kelverstoke, a fictional city in a UK-like island state

layer1: offence records whose occurrence time is a window (occurred_from and occurred_to) and whose report time is a third timestamp
two recording systems across the window, the force's legacy incident export to March 2026 and the new records management system after it, with different column names and time formats
the same offence present in both exports across the cut-over fortnight under two reference numbers
a licensed premises register whose addresses match the offence locations only through a gazetteer with two spellings per street
night-time economy footfall counts from four pedestrian sensors with gaps where a sensor was down
a patrol tasking plan in a spreadsheet, one sheet per quarter, hours written as text
offences recorded under a British Summer Time local clock across two clock changes
an offence class whose counts jump when a national counting rule changed, documented in the extract notes
driver: The decisive quantity is a rate over the positions of a cycle, and each record's position is known only within a window whose placement is set by an observer's own routine rather than by the event, so a likelihood treating the window as uninformative piles mass into the positions just before the routine's notice points, and the obvious fit, however well converged, reorders the cycle wrongly.
driver_concrete: Each offence's hour has to be estimated from a window bounded by when the keeper last looked and when the keeper first noticed, and those bounds cluster at opening, closing and shift times by premises type, so the hours nobody looks at are represented only through the windows that end at the next look; the hour-of-week profile has to be fitted against each premises type's own notice distribution, and the uninformative-window fit reorders the week.
stump: A competent analyst fits the weekly profile by maximum likelihood over the occurrence windows, treating each window as uninformative about the hour inside it, and files a slate in which Thursday and Friday daytime slots displace two genuine late-night slots, because the windows end at the keepers' notice times and the fit reads that pile-up as offending.
analyst_test: A strong analyst reads every field correctly, sees that four in five offences carry an occurrence window rather than a time, refuses the window start, end and midpoint and refuses flat spreading, and fits the weekly profile by maximum likelihood over the interval-censored windows to its own fixed point, treating each window as uninformative about the hour inside it; that likelihood piles mass into the hours just before the common notice times, so it files a slate whose Thursday and Friday daytime slots displace two genuine late-night slots.
domain_test: The deciding quantity is the offence rate by hour of the week over a recorded-crime series whose occurrence times are interval-censored, which criminology estimates with an interval-censored hazard or a latent-clock fit and judges against the observability of each hour; swap the nouns to megawatt-hours or clinic visits and the task breaks, because neither has a keeper whose routine decides when the event can be noticed, so neither has a window whose placement carries information about the hour inside it.

differentiation.task184: architecture 2 made the decisive step a choice of estimation GROUPING, one clock across the five offence classes against one per class, which stumping 1.1c closes from both horns and whose judge failed it on Gate C at z = -4.29; and its step moved only the cap boundary, so its reader got seven of the eight slots (stumping 1.1d). Architecture 3 keeps the world, the pack, the ask layer and the latent-clock mechanism and changes what is estimated: the window's PLACEMENT is informative about the hour inside it, so the naive likelihood is misspecified rather than merely grouped at the wrong level, and the correction reorders the week globally instead of at the cap.
differentiation.task464: the shared axes are the generic ones (a population gap, no pattern, Gate G method selection, a ranked slate under a cap). task464 links two measurement SCALES: part of the population was read on an old instrument, a both-ways sample links the scales, and predicting each unit's new value by regression shrinks the converted spread so the tail past the cut is too thin. Nothing there is censored in time and nothing depends on an observer's routine; here each record's POSITION IN A CYCLE is known only within a window an observer's routine placed, so the correction is to the likelihood's censoring mechanism rather than to an attenuated scale, and the quantity reordered is a weekly profile rather than a tail count.

lineage.fate: spent 2026-10-14: judge SEND_BACK at the hardening (Gate C, the forward lanes are not filed, so the counterfactual arm is inferred from last summer; Gate G surface_read_rejection, the difficulty is the refusal of an official artifact). Shipped 10-12 as the single-layer version and left off the portal's approved list.
lineage.driver: The decisive quantity is what a shared resource adds to a site, and both arms of that difference are taken from the site's own filed plan when the site's records show it never meets the plan: the untreated arm has to be read from what the site does on its own, and the shortfall its treated periods show against the plan has to be split into the part the resource caused and the part that was there anyway, so subtracting the whole shortfall while keeping the plan as the untreated arm, the obvious correction, ranks the sites wrongly too.
lineage.stump: A competent solver runs the planning standard on each airport's 2027 design days and summer roster pattern with the unit's three lanes added and posts the unit to Cullinvale (697,500 passengers moved within the standard); the step that lands it there is taking the roster pattern as the lanes that will be open on both arms of the comparison, when the checkpoints' own lane counts show seven of the eight opening fewer lanes at their banks than the pattern plans on every day of the summer, Eskerford two fewer, so the posting moves the most at Eskerford (342,200).
lineage.niche: posting a national screening agency's one mobile screening unit to one of eight flagged airports for the summer, judged by the passengers it moves within the 20-minute queue standard, when host airports stand down their own lanes while the unit is there
lineage.answer: Post the mobile screening unit to Eskerford from 15 June to 31 August 2027: it moves 342,200 passengers within the 20-minute standard, against 272,600 at Halloran Bay, and 13 per cent is the smallest whole per cent shortfall in Eskerford's forecast passengers at which another posting would move more.

lineage.fate: spent 2026-10-25 on measurement, not on a portal result. Its judge failed Gate C (underspecified_objective) with Gate F strong and Gates G and H passing: one clock per offence class gives seven of the eight slots and a different eighth, totalling 4,866 a season against 5,705, at a likelihood ratio of per-class over pooled of 511.1 on 668 degrees of freedom, z = -4.29, so the data neither reject pooling nor prefer it. A blind reader then fitted per class unasked and filed 5,096.6 with the same two slots swapped, missing all seven call figures and taking 31.7 per cent of the asks (a pair of 29.4, under the 40 target). Closed by stumping 1.1c and 1.1d: a grouping choice is not drawable, and a step that bites only at the cap makes Gate F and Gate C the same margin.
lineage.driver: The decisive quantity is a latent cyclical profile recovered from records that observe each event only as the interval it fell in, where the interval is the gap in the target's own inspection routine and its length varies systematically with the part of the cycle it covers, so the flat reading that spreads each event evenly across its own interval divides the busiest parts of the cycle across the longest intervals and the quietest across the shortest, and only the placement under which the recorded intervals are the likeliest set to have been recorded recovers the profile.
lineage.stump: The default path spreads each occurrence window evenly over its own hours and commissions Friday 12:00 to 16:00, Thursday 20:00 to 00:00, Friday 00:00 to 04:00, Saturday 00:00 to 04:00, Friday 16:00 to 20:00, Thursday 16:00 to 20:00, Friday 20:00 to 00:00 and Sunday 20:00 to 00:00, filing 3,150 covered offences a season, when its eight meet only 4,250 of the golden's 5,700; the step that lands it there is reading the window as a claim that the offence is equally likely in each of its hours, when the window is the keeper's own closure and the closures covering the heaviest nights are the longest.
